correctness.rationale: In the diameter-two rook graph a forbidden triple consists exactly of the two consecutive legs of a right angle with its nonadjacent endpoints. Double occupancy in column j uses two rows that cannot then appear in any other column, so no second column can have double occupancy. Double-occupancy faces not containing a full column therefore belong to the stated thickening simplex, while a full column is isolated from all other cells. Two different thickenings intersect only in the column-thin complex A_n; the intersection of any individual thickening with A_n is S^0 joined with the nonempty simplex of allowed cells in the remaining columns, hence contractible. Cofibration gluing proves that A_n includes by a homotopy equivalence into the thickened core. Joining three-point spaces, starting with K_{3,3}, doubles the wedge rank and suspends at each stage; the core is therefore simply connected for n≥3 and has 2^n spheres in degree n−1. Each of the n column triangles attaches along its three edges already in the core by a nullhomotopic boundary map. The homotopy pushout splits off n two-spheres relative to the core up to homotopy, so the actual A_n inclusion induces an integral homology summand even at n=3, where the total rank in degree two is 11. Both sides are connected, giving the ordinary H_0 assertion as well.
residual_risks: No assertion for the two-column case, other row counts, or equivariant equivalence; recorded finite checks are not the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The maximum size is not homotopy data. For three rows and at least three columns, rook nonadjacency is not transitive on distinct related cells, so the graph is not complete multipartite. The categorical product is not the Cartesian rook graph; a coincident count at n=3 does not establish coverage.
